title: FEHA criminal history and source-of-income screening protections
requirement: Landlords may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and may not blanket-ban applicants with criminal history. Conviction-based denial must be directly related to tenancy, and source-of-income discrimination, including refusing Section 8 vouchers, is barred.
coverage_conditions: Most housing accommodations in California and most housing providers, including landlords, tenant screening companies, apartment managers, and property management companies.

applicability.per_tenancy: An owner occupying the home and renting to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics.

penalty: Remedies include out-of-pocket losses, injunctions, access to housing, emotional distress damages, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney’s fees.
citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
interaction: FEHA invalidates any state law to the extent it purports to require or permit unlawful housing discrimination.
